characterization_methods.key_findings: M1-SS exhibits coarse equiaxed austenite grains with straight annealing-twin lamellae and thin dark grain boundaries; average grain size 42.4 ± 7.8 μm, unchanged after 30 h aging.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 200× magnification; samples etched with 3 % FeCl3 + 10 % HCl (in ethanol) for 10–20 s; section parallel to rolled surface; grain size measured per GB/T 6394-2002
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase morphology characterization and grain size measurement

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Thermo Fisher Scientific Talos F200X G2
characterization_methods.key_findings: M1-SS austenite matrix is uniform and precipitate-free; only dark straight/curved boundary lines meeting at a triple junction are visible, no second-phase particles. Since Cr and Mo do not precipitate at the solution temperature, no precipitates form in the M1 matrix.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: BF imaging; TEM foils mechanically ground to 50 μm, 3 mm discs punched and ion-thinned to electron transparency
characterization_methods.purpose: To examine the matrix and detect any precipitates in the solution-treated M1 steel

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SUNS UTM5105X electronic universal testing machine; 12.5 mm extensometer
characterization_methods.key_findings: Solution-treated M1 steel yield strength approximately 430 MPa; tensile/strain-hardening curves reported in Fig. 7 and Fig. 11.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; specimens 2 mm thick, 58 mm long fabricated along rolling direction; ground with SiC papers; 0.2 % offset yield definition
characterization_methods.purpose: To measure the mechanical properties (yield strength, tensile behaviour) of M1-SS

analytical_models.model_note: ΔG_ex = 170.06 exp(−D/18.55) (Eq. 9); Ti and V have little influence on the SFE. Calculated SFE of M1 ≈ 70 mJ/m².

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated SFE of M1 (~70 mJ/m²) indicates dislocation-slip-dominated deformation, consistent with observed planar dislocation slip after tensile testing.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Applied to M1 and M2 (conditions M1-SS, M1-30, M2-SS, M2-30 in Fig. 10); dislocation strengthening neglected because both steels underwent high-temperature solution treatment.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: In the solution-treated state, the Ti/V-modified M2 steel (M2-SS) exhibited a ~200 MPa higher yield strength than the Ti/V-free M1-SS; M1-SS is the lower-strength reference.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The Ti/V-free M1 low-density steel was melted in a high-vacuum electric-arc melting furnace (composition: Fe bal., 20.17 Mn, 8.12 Al, 0.61 C, 0.17 Si, 0.40 Cr, 0.31 Mo, no V or Ti).
Prehistory of the M1-SS condition: ingots hot rolled from 20 to 2 mm at 1000 °C then water quenched.

Solution-processed at 1000 °C for 30 min then water quenched; the two solution-treated steels were named M1-SS and M2-SS. In the Ti/V-free M1, no precipitates form at this temperature (Cr and Mo do not precipitate at the solution temperature).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Specimens fabricated along the rolling direction; 12.5 mm extensometer used to measure gauge-length deformation; yield strength determined at a 0.2 % offset.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: 2 mm thick, 58 mm long tensile specimens

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–engineering strain curve and true stress–true strain / strain-hardening-rate curve for M1-SS (black dotted curves) are reported in Fig. 7; M1-SS shows the lowest strength level of the four conditions.

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with straight annealing-twin lamellae

structures.overall_structure: Equiaxed austenite (γ, FCC) grains with straight annealing-twin lamellae and thin dark grain boundaries; single-phase austenite matrix of the Ti/V-free M1 steel after solution treatment at 1000 °C/30 min, with no observable intragranular precipitates.

unmapped_findings: M1-SS is the solution-treated state of the Ti/V-free Fe–Mn–Al–C austenitic low-density steel (composition: Fe bal., 20.17 Mn, 8.12 Al, 0.61 C, 0.17 Si, 0.40 Cr, 0.31 Mo; V and Ti not added, shown as '–' in Table 1). [b0016, b0026]

For M1-SS, Cr and Mo do not precipitate at the solution temperature (1000 °C), so no precipitates are observed within the austenite matrix; unlike the Ti/V-added M2-SS, the M1-SS matrix is precipitate-free (Fig. 3a). [b0030, figure_003]
The κ-carbide and (Ti,V)C quantification table gives dashes for all M1-SS entries, i.e. neither (Ti,V)C nor κ-carbide is present/quantified in the solution-treated M1 steel. [figure_unlabelled_002]
The average grain size of M1-SS is 42.4 ± 7.8 μm (Table 2); 30 h aging (M1-30) does not significantly change it (45.3 ± 9.3 μm). [b0028, table_002]
The stacking fault energy (SFE) of M1 steel, calculated by the Olson–Cohen model, is approximately 70 mJ/m², indicating that the deformation mode is dislocation slip. [b0084, b0088]
The work-hardening behaviour of M1-SS is divided into three stages (Stage I, Stage II, Stage III), whereas after aging only two stages are observed. [b0091, figure_011]
In M1 the κ-carbides precipitate only after aging (M1-30) and precipitate uniformly in the matrix; in the solution-treated state (M1-SS) they are absent. [b0031, b0034, b0056]
